diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)\leq 1$, (\ref{e_ortho}) can only hold if all factors $\sigma_j(\mc)/\sigma_1(\mc)=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only gives equality of all singular values, i.e. \mc^T\mc=\sigma_1(\mc)^2 I_k. Without the unit-norm-column hypothesis this means orthogonal columns of equal norm, not necessarily orthonormal columns. The reductions use submatrices of a unit-norm-column matrix, where (\ref{e_srk}) forces \sigma_1=1 and the applications are valid, but the lemma as stated is false.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis \|\mc\ve_j\|_2=1 for the equality part, or replace 'orthonormal' by 'orthogonal columns with equal norm'.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone optimal-value characterization of relative volume is incorrect for general full-column-rank matrices; the later uses inside unit-norm-column reductions remain usable after adding the missing hypothesis.
issues.title: Relative-volume equality characterization is false without unit-norm columns
issues.why_classification: A single local hypothesis or equality-condition correction restores the exact intended statement without changing any rate, threshold, or subsequent reduction.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract's phrase 'these criteria' is attached to a list that includes Frobenius-norm minimization, which the paper itself says is polynomial-time solvable, and Schatten p-norm criteria for p>2, for which the paper says a PTAS gap was not obtained. The paper proves no PTAS only for the subset of criteria listed in Table 1 with a nonblank No PTAS entry.

failure_location.quote: do not admit polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract sentence so that NP hardness and no-PTAS are asserted only for the criteria actually proved, separating the polynomial-time Frobenius-norm case and the p>2 Schatten cases for which only NP hardness is claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the PTAS-inapproximability contribution is materially larger than the proved scope.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims PTAS inapproximability for all listed criteria

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,3M\}$ and a collection of distinct subsets

issues.failure_explanation: The reduction never verifies the required hypothesis rank(A)>=M. A valid X3C no-instance can violate it: take M=6, universe {1,...,18}, and let the collection consist of the ten distinct 3-subsets of a fixed five-element subset. There is no exact cover, but the incidence matrix has rank at most 5<M, so the constructed instance is outside the stated rank(A)>=k domain and the volume/pseudo-inverse/condition formulations have no rank-M submatrix to optimize over.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair is identified for the promised rank(A)>=k class. At minimum, either prove a rank-preserving reduction from the stated X3C problem, or redefine the decision problems to accept rank-deficient matrices and specify the no/infeasible value; the latter proves hardness for an extended problem rather than the advertised restricted class.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the polynomial-time reduction does not map every X3C no-instance to a legal instance of the stated decision problems, so the reduction-based NP-hardness and threshold statements for the promised rank(A)>=k class are not established for those no-instances.
issues.title: X3C reduction can leave the stated rank(A) >= k instance domain
issues.why_classification: The counterexample is concrete and defeats the instance hypothesis for a family of no-instances; preserving the advertised rank(A)>=k scope appears to require a new rank-preserving construction, while simply dropping the rank promise changes the stated problem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.
For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that
Assume that X3C instance is false, and assume that any two columns of $\mc$ overlap.

issues.failure_explanation: A false X3C instance guarantees only that every M-column choice contains at least one overlapping pair. Proper subcollections may be disjoint: for M>2, two disjoint sets have volume 1, two-norm 1, pseudo-inverse two-norm 1, and pseudo-inverse Frobenius-square 2, so the displayed induction hypotheses fail for exactly the disjoint subcollections the induction quantifies over. The same gap is used in the two-norm, pseudo-inverse two-norm, and pseudo-inverse Frobenius inductions.

failure_location.quote: For matrices $\hat{\mc}_{k-1}$ with $k-1$ columns, assume that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the arbitrary-count induction by a reduction to an overlapping pair: order or partition the columns so an overlapping pair is isolated, then use column-removal, singular-value interlacing, or Lemma l_fi for the Frobenius pseudo-inverse case.
issues.overall_effect: The proofs do not establish the stated lower/upper bounds for all false X3C instances; the dependent thresholds obtained from them, including S-optimality, mixed condition, Schatten pseudo-inverse, Frobenius condition, and stable rank, inherit the gap.
issues.title: False-X3C inductions ignore disjoint proper subcollections
issues.why_classification: The conclusions and thresholds survive, but the repair is not a single added hypothesis; each affected proof needs a contained replacement argument using the guaranteed overlapping pair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.failure_explanation: The factors (2sqrt(2)/3)^(1/k) and sqrt(1+1/(4k)) tend to 1 as k grows. For a fixed epsilon, they beat the PTAS ratio 1+epsilon or 1-epsilon only for bounded k. Because the reduction uses distinct 3-subsets of a 3k-element universe, bounding k also bounds the number of possible columns by binomial(3k,3), so these bounded-k cases do not provide an unbounded family of instances hard at the fixed PTAS ratio. Thus the proved gap statement is weaker than the asserted 'no PTAS' conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: A complete repair must supply a constant-factor gap, or otherwise for every epsilon produce an unbounded instance family whose gap exceeds 1+epsilon for minimization and 1-epsilon for maximization; the source provides no such argument, so these four no-PTAS statements must be withdrawn or reproved.
issues.overall_effect: The S-optimality, Frobenius pseudo-inverse, Schatten p pseudo-inverse, and Frobenius condition no-PTAS claims are unsupported by the stated arguments, even if their k-dependent bounds are repaired.
issues.title: Closing k-dependent approximation gaps do not imply no PTAS
issues.why_classification: The defect removes the central PTAS conclusion for four criteria rather than merely weakening a proof step; the stated k-dependent hardness does not convert into inapproximability within any fixed PTAS ratio.
